```json
{"ranking": ["R2", "C2", "Cc"], "fault": "Most likely R2 is about 10x too small (originally ~113 kOhm). Two other faults could cause this, so the ranking is uncertain."}
```

**Main clue: the passive network doesn't match the target.** With an ideal op-amp, the RC network as listed gives:

- Natural frequency: 1/(2π·√(R1·R2·C1·C2)) ≈ 1.25 GHz.
- Q: √(R1·R2·C1·C2) / (C2·(R1+R2)) ≈ 1.04.
- That puts the −3 dB point near 1.6 GHz, about 8x above the 152–228 MHz window.

The measured fc of 224 MHz therefore isn't set by the filter. It comes from the op-amp's closed-loop limit, which is low:

- Op-amp unity-gain bandwidth: gm1/Cc ≈ 267 µS / 143 fF ≈ 300 MHz.
- The pole at the M3/M4 mirror node also sits around 270 MHz, by my rough estimate.
- So the buffer has poor phase margin right around the measured fc.

That explains the 14 dB peaking. It also explains why every sensitivity listed is an op-amp element (M4, Cc, M3, M5).

**Why R2.** A single passive change has to bring the natural frequency down to a few hundred MHz and lower Q, so the filter rolls off before the op-amp's marginal region. The fit for each candidate:

| Candidate (scaled 10x) | Natural freq. | Q | Est. fc | Fits? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| R2 ≈ 113 kΩ | ≈ 394 MHz | ≈ 0.37 | ≈ 165 MHz | Yes, centred in spec |
| C2 ≈ 96 fF | ≈ 394 MHz | ≈ 0.33 | ≈ 150 MHz | Borderline |
| R1 larger | — | ≈ 1.6 | — | No, Q goes up |
| C1 larger | — | ≈ 3.3 | — | No, Q goes up |

The "10x" factor is an assumption I tried, not something I derived. The fc estimates ignore the op-amp. The R2/R1 ratio this implies (about 75) is unusual for a design.

**Cc as an alternative.** I ranked it third because the sensitivities show a larger Cc reduces peaking. A Cc corrupted upward would therefore help rather than hurt, so this fault is less likely.

**M5 being in triode is probably not the fault.** The tail node sits at 0.224 V because of the input common-mode (about 0.9 V) minus M1's Vgs. M6 runs every NMOS in the bias network at a Vdsat around 0.55 V. With that setup, any M5 width would be close to triode.
